article_title: Integrating augmented reality into inquiry-based learning approach in primary science classrooms
citation: Wen, Y., Wu, L., He, S., Ng, N. H.-E., Teo, B. C., Looi, C. K., & Cai, Y. (2023). Integrating augmented reality into inquiry-based learning approach in primary science classrooms. Education Tech Research Dev, 71, 1631–1651. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-023-10235-y
title: QIMS: an inquiry-based learning framework for leveraging the affordances of AR
description: QIMS is an inquiry-based learning framework proposed by the authors to leverage the affordances of augmented reality in teaching and learning. The article states that "In leveraging the affordances of AR, an inquiry-based learning framework, referred to as QIMS, was proposed in this study." It was operationalised into a learning package on plant reproduction for primary 5 students and evaluated against non-QIMS conditions.
requirements: Implementation requires a learning package designed on the QIMS framework, as the study developed its lessons on the topic of plant reproduction based on QIMS
constraints: Evaluated in primary science lessons with students aged 11–12; the article notes many existing studies neglected pedagogy and instructional models when implementing AR
target_learning_goals: 21st-century skills: self-directed learning, creative thinking, critical thinking, knowledge creation efficacy
examples: A learning package on plant reproduction for primary 5 students was developed based on the QIMS framework and tested in a three-condition quasi-experiment
key_sources: Wen, Y., Wu, L., He, S., Ng, N. H.-E., Teo, B. C., Looi, C. K., & Cai, Y. (2023). Integrating augmented reality into inquiry-based learning approach in primary science classrooms. Education Tech Research Dev, 71, 1631–1651. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-023-10235-y

article_title: Integrating augmented reality into inquiry-based learning approach in primary science classrooms

title: Plant reproduction learning package for primary 5 students built on the QIMS framework
description: A learning package developed on the topic of plant reproduction for primary 5 students (aged 11–12), designed based on the QIMS inquiry-based framework. The article states it was developed "on the topic of plant reproduction for primary 5 students (aged 11–12) based on the QIMS framework" and served as the instructional material in the three-condition quasi-experiment.
requirements: Lessons implemented as a series of science lessons in a primary school under the QIMS framework
constraints: Designed for the primary 5 plant reproduction topic; evaluated in one primary school
examples: The package was used across three conditions (AR and QIMS; QIMS; Non-AR and Non-QIMS) with 117 students

article_title: Engaging ESP University Students in Flipped Classrooms for Developing Functional Writing Skills, HOTs, and Eliminating Writer's Block
citation: Salem, A. A. M. S. (2018). Engaging ESP University Students in Flipped Classrooms for Developing Functional Writing Skills, HOTs, and Eliminating Writer's Block. English Language Teaching, 11(12). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v11n12p177
title: Questionnaire for Identifying Writer's Block (QIWB)
description: The QIWB, developed by Rose (1981), is "an attitude questionnaire of 24 items that are divided into 5 subscales": Blocking, Lateness, premature editing, strategies for complexity, and attitudes. It rests on the assumption that writer's block reflects not only emotional response to fear of evaluation but also cognitive difficulties such as lacking strategies for composing complex discourse or editing too early. Administrators wishing to identify only blockers can administer just the behavioral subscales (blocking and lateness). The article reports a total Cronbach's alpha of .74 and dimension correlation coefficients from .455 to .905 supporting reliability and validity.
requirements: Reliability upon multiple administration, as reported in Table 5, to assess writer's block levels with considerable confidence
constraints: The article presents it as assessing writer's block rather than related constructs such as writing apprehension or writing anxiety
target_learning_goals: identifying and assessing writer's block levels
examples: The study used the QIWB as a pre and post measure of writer's block for both experimental and control groups.
key_sources: Salem, A. A. M. S. (2018). Engaging ESP University Students in Flipped Classrooms for Developing Functional Writing Skills, HOTs, and Eliminating Writer's Block. English Language Teaching, 11(12). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v11n12p177

article_title: Transferring skills in quality collaboratives focused on improving patient logistics.
citation: Weggelaar-Jansen AM, van Wijngaarden J. (2018). Transferring skills in quality collaboratives focused on improving patient logistics. BMC Health Services Research. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12913-018-3051-8
title: Quality improvement collaborative (QIC) as an educational model combining learning sessions, change packages, extranet sharing and on-site support
description: The article describes the QIC as an improvement-and-education method in which, per Øvretveit et al. as quoted, "a collaborative [that] brings together groups of practitioners from different healthcare organizations to work in a structured way to improve a specific aspect of the quality of their service." Most QICs use the IHI Breakthrough methodology. The studied QICs' educational approach organized learning sessions taught by change experts and subject experts, supported by change packages (booklets describing ten distinctive phases with PowerPoint files and communication tools), a collaborative extranet, and QIC staff site visits.
requirements: Series of structured meetings to learn best practices, quality methods and change topics, and to share experiences of local changes
constraints: The studied QICs focused on patient logistics: Advanced Access aimed to reduce outpatient access time to a maximum of two days; Process Redesign aimed to reduce throughput time for admitted patients by at least 20%
target_learners: healthcare professionals in hospitals participating in quality improvement collaboratives
target_learning_goals: identifying and resolving bottlenecks in patient flow
examples: Twenty-four of approximately 110 Dutch hospitals participated in three tranches; the studied QICs ran for five years.
key_sources: Weggelaar-Jansen AM, van Wijngaarden J. (2018). Transferring skills in quality collaboratives focused on improving patient logistics. BMC Health Services Research. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12913-018-3051-8
